answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity gets a persistent thread of signed action logs; a verifier samples behaviour across epochs and requires continuity of role, timing, and counterparties. Agents whose histories wander between unrelated tasks lose reputation weight. The rule is enforced through a trellis of epoch checkpoints: missed or contradictory links block rewards. An attacker must run and maintain a believable, costly history per identity across many epochs, multiplying effort linearly with the number of fake identities.
